transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm here because when I’m alone working late, I start eating and it feels like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating until it’s over. It's really starting to overwhelm me, and I don't know how to make it stop.
After these episodes of eating, do you feel a strong urge to use methods like self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or laxatives to prevent weight gain?
No, I don't do any of those things, and I've never felt the urge to try them. After it happens, I just feel incredibly full and miserable, but I don't try to throw up or use laxatives.
Beyond these episodes of eating, have you been experiencing a persistent low mood, loss of interest in activities, or feelings of worthlessness for most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say I have a constant, daily low mood or feel worthless. While I have been skipping social plans and hobbies like hiking, it's really just because I feel so sluggish, ashamed, and drained the day after one of these late-night eating episodes.
During these late-night episodes, do you find yourself eating significantly faster than normal or eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yes, both of those are definitely true. I eat incredibly fast, barely chewing or tasting the food before swallowing, just rushing through it. And I don't stop until my stomach is so painfully tight and bloated that it hurts to even sit up straight in my desk chair.
On average, how many times per week do these episodes of eating large amounts of food occur, and has this been happening for at least three months?

Yes, it has been happening for about ten months now, starting a few months after I got my promotion. On average, I have these episodes at least once a week, but it can happen even more often when my work deadlines start piling up.
